sentences.text: [deadpan, dry humor] Your phone's at nine percent, and the emperor of Rome wants a miracle.
This emperor, legend says, pranked his dinner guests with cushions that slowly let the air out.
So you play him a fart sound.
Then the flashlight, and fifty thousand people gasp.
So he asks the crowd: should the stranger live?
The thumbs go up, and you throw two thumbs up right back.
In Rome, a thumb up may have meant: kill him.
Thumbs down for death comes from a painting, made over sixteen hundred years later.
Mercy was a thumb hidden in your fist.
And you're still giving everyone two thumbs up.
[after a long pause] [lowering their voice] Comment ARENA for part three.
